Tucson, Arizona · eat

Restaurants in Tucson for cyclists

Where to eat in Tucson the night before and the afternoon after. Real food, open when you need it.

For: El Tour de Tucson.

Restaurants in Tucson for cyclists, listed

  1. Seis Kitchen (Mercado San Agustín)

    • Mexican
    • 130 S Avenida del Convento #100, Tucson, AZ 85745

    Nearby ride: Women’s Shootout Tucson (Saturdays, 7:15 am) →

    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Seis Kitchen (Mercado San Agustín)

    After the ride, west side: in the Mercado San Agustín courtyard where the Women’s Shootout (Saturdays, 7:15 am) meets, less than half a mile from the Loop. Breakfast from 8, until 11 on weekdays and noon on weekends, then lunch and dinner to 9. No reservations; you order, then they seat you, per its site. (520) 622-2002.

  2. 5 Points Restaurant

    • Brunch
    • 756 S Stone Ave, Tucson, AZ 85701
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about 5 Points Restaurant

    After the ride, just south of downtown in Barrio Viejo and a short way from the convention center hotels: brunch 9 to 2 and dinner 5 to 9, Thursday to Monday, closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Book on Resy, patio tables too; dogs are welcome on the patio, and its site says it is easy to reach by bike. (520) 623-3888.

  3. Cup Cafe at Hotel Congress

    After the ride, downtown: the café inside Hotel Congress, with a dining room and a patio that runs out into the hotel’s plaza.

    • American cafe
    • 311 E Congress St, Tucson, AZ 85701
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Cup Cafe at Hotel Congress

    No reservations for breakfast or lunch, per its page. The page gave no hours when we checked in October 2026; confirm before you go.

  4. El Charro Café (Downtown)

    The night before, downtown.

    • Sonoran Mexican
    • 311 N Court Ave, Tucson, AZ 85701
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about El Charro Café (Downtown)

    Open 11 to 9 every day, and it takes reservations, so a group can book ahead, per its site. (520) 622-1922.

  5. BOCA by Chef Maria Mazon

    The night before, or late on a weekend, on Fourth Avenue: tacos on corn or flour tortillas with the house salsas, cooked to order.

    • Tacos
    • 533 N 4th Ave, Tucson, AZ 85705
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about BOCA by Chef Maria Mazon

    Noon to 9 Monday to Thursday, to 10 Friday and Saturday, to 8 Sunday, per its site. 520-777-8134.

  6. El Güero Canelo (Oracle)

    Late, north of downtown on Oracle Road: Sonoran hot dogs, carne asada tacos and burros from a James Beard Award-winning restaurant, per its site.

    • Sonoran hot dogs
    • 2480 N Oracle Rd, Tucson, AZ 85705
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about El Güero Canelo (Oracle)

    11 to 10, and to 11 on Friday and Saturday. The two other locations, on East 22nd Street and South 12th Avenue, close at 10. (520) 882-8977.

  7. Tumerico

    The meat-free pick, midtown on Sixth Street: vegetarian and vegan Latin American plates.

    • Latin vegan
    • 2526 E 6th St, Tucson, AZ 85716
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Tumerico

    11 to 8 Tuesday to Saturday, 10 to 4 Sunday, closed Monday, per its site, so it is an early dinner. 520-240-6947.

  8. Barrio Bread

    The one you’d go back for: Don Guerra’s bakery.

    • Bakery
    • 18 S Eastbourne Ave, Tucson, AZ 85716
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Barrio Bread

    He won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Baker in 2022, per its site. Open 9 to 1 every day, or until it sells out, so go in the morning. 520-327-1292.
